Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week — team is excited to move forward. Our procurement group asked me to confirm a few operational details before we issue the official PO:

- Required PO fields: we need a single PO number that appears on every invoice line and on the invoice header (our ERP reconciles on that).
- Invoice cutoff: our AP team prefers a weekly invoice release (Friday close) but can also accept monthly consolidated invoices if there is an agreed pre-auth stub to reconcile during the month.
- Net terms: default is Net 60 for new vendors; we can move to Net 45 for strategic partners with a short credit check.

I've attached our standard PO template (Novus_PO_template.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can: (1) include the PO number on every invoice line, (2) support weekly or monthly consolidated invoices, and (3) accept Net 45 under an enterprise onboarding exception?

If you can sketch a suggested invoicing pattern that fits your billing ops, that will help speed up legal/procurement.

Thanks,

Hi Olivia — appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front: yes, yes, and likely yes with a quick credit sync. Details below.

Quick operational options we support:
1) Weekly pulse + monthly settlement: we can run a weekly invoice "stub" (summary CSV) every Friday that lists token/usage lines with a single monthly consolidation invoice processed on the 1st of the next month. The weekly stubs are informational and can be used by AP for reconciliation.
2) True weekly invoices: we can support issuing invoices weekly with the PO number on the header and every line. This requires us to enable a weekly billing run in our finance system (no technical blocker).
3) Monthly consolidated invoice: single invoice with all line items; PO number on every line — default for most enterprise customers.

Net terms: our standard self-serve contracts are Net 30. For dedicated/enterprise customers we can offer Net 45 pending finance review; Net 60 is possible with a signed commitment and an internal credit exception (takes ~5–7 business days).

PO formatting: we will ensure the PO id is included as an invoice-level field and echoed at line-level in our export file (CSV/PDF). Please confirm the exact header name you need (e.g., "PO Number", "Purchase Order ID", or your internal PO field).

I've attached our onboarding checklist and a sample stub export so your AP can see the line format (redwood-po-onboarding-checklist.xlsx, redwood-monthly-stub-example.csv).

Next steps: if Novus can accept the weekly-stub + monthly-settlement option, we can proceed with a PO issuance and I will kick off the finance exception for Net 45. If you prefer weekly invoices, please confirm so I can scope the billing-run change.

Thanks — looping Vanessa and Priyom to confirm finance/ops details.

Best,
Markus Klein

Hi Olivia — Vanessa here (billing ops). A couple practical notes from our side that usually speed procurement approvals: 

- Compromise approach we recommend: weekly informational stubs + a single monthly invoice. The stub contains per-route and per-model lines so your AP can tag spend details without processing multiple payments. The monthly invoice carries the single payable amount.
- PO identifier: please confirm you want the header field labeled exactly as "Purchase Order ID". If so we'll map that to both PDF and CSV outputs.
- Early-pay discount: we can offer a 2% discount on the consolidated monthly invoice if Novus agrees to pay within 10 days (Net 10 early-pay). This is optional but helpful if you want to shorten cash conversion.
- Credit/Net terms: to get Net 45 we need a completed vendor credit form (two fields: legal entity tax ID + bank reference). Once we have that finance will approve within 3 business days in most cases.

If this sounds acceptable I can prepare a short SOW describing the invoicing pattern and discount option (1 page) and a DocuSign envelope for signatures.

Vanessa Ortiz
